omissions: Text extraction does not reconstruct figure images; inspect the retained PDF for figures and equation/table layout.
Separate supplemental material availability has not been fully verified.

The extraction limitation was addressed by inspecting all scientific figure/table pages and all six final crops. All six supplied text chunks, including references and appendices, were read without truncation.

Identity/version notes: exact title and all seven author names agree with the catalog. Reviewed arXiv:2606.13515v1; the sidebar says 11 June 2026 and the title block says 12 June 2026. No other revision was supplied.
The title page assigns Chenghao Gu affiliation marker 4, but lists institutions only under 1–3. The institution names are verified collectively; his individual affiliation remains unresolved.
No external project, code, checkpoints or separate supplements were inspected; no experiments were reproduced.

synopsis: MaskWAM couples RGB and mask future prediction with action denoising, using an optional first-frame target mask to resolve ambiguous instructions. Its central empirical distinction is between supplying a mask and training the policy to predict its future: the latter substantially improves mask-guided robot execution in the evaluated setup. Deployment uses partially denoised visual latents, while fully decoded future videos are offline illustrations (joint, inference, ablation).

problem.text: RGB prediction can spend representational capacity on irrelevant backgrounds, while language may not distinguish similar objects in clutter. The authors therefore seek both object-focused predictive supervision and an explicit target-selection interface, retaining ordinary text-conditioned operation for unambiguous tasks.

contributions.text: A shared visual latent stream predicts RGB and task-relevant masks, interacting with a separate action expert through MoT attention.
First-frame mask dropout permits prompted and unprompted operation; mask prediction is presented as the mechanism that makes the prompt useful.

outputs: Future RGB I_{1:T} and masks M_{1:T} as predictive targets; deployment uses their intermediate latents

steps.name: Render and encode masks
steps.detail: Render task masks as three-channel images with fixed object/background colors. Encode masks and RGB using the same causal 3D VAE, preserving alignment in temporal horizon and spatial resolution.

steps.name: Fuse in the video latent space
steps.detail: Concatenate RGB and mask latents by channel. Expand the pretrained patch embedding from C to 2C channels, preserving RGB weights and zero-initializing added mask weights; expand the prediction head correspondingly.

steps.name: Couple visual and action experts
steps.detail: Wan 2.2 supplies the visual backbone. T5 language features enter its cross-attention; projected proprioception and noisy actions enter the action expert. Figure 2 permits actions to attend visual context while blocking visual queries from action/state keys.

training.text: Fine-tune the prediction model while freezing the video VAE and T5. RGB and masks share noise timestep τ_v; actions use independent τ_a, exposing action denoising to multiple visual noise levels. Sum video, mask and action flow losses. Initial masks are zeroed with probability 0.5.

Reported inputs are 384 × 320 T-shape RGB frames with future horizon T = 8. Training labels use Qwen3-VL/SAM3 for language-clear episodes and human first-frame points for ambiguous episodes, followed by SAM3 propagation and human correction.

inference.text: Obtain an optional SAM3 mask once at episode start. At a prediction call, condition on current RGB, language and proprioception, take one RGB-mask denoising step, and generate the action chunk using cached visual context. Subsequent predictions do not require repeated segmentation prompts.

Predicted action chunks drive real-robot evaluation. Full future RGB/mask decoding in Figure 10 is explicitly offline; those images do not establish test-time video rollout planning. Exact action execution cadence and sampler settings are unspecified.

equations.explanation: Eq. (1) defines joint future/action prediction. I denotes RGB observations, M masks, s_0 proprioception and ℓ language; K is action chunk size, T the future-frame horizon, and D the action dimension in the source's action tensor.
Eq. (2) concatenates RGB latent z_v and mask latent z_m along channels. C, L, H′ and W′ are latent channel count, temporal length, height and width.
Eq. (3) sums the source-defined flow-matching losses for RGB video, masks and action trajectories. Visual and action timesteps are sampled independently.

results.setting: Four benchmark suites; language-conditioned deployment without visual prompts.
results.interpretation: The RGB-only difference is 1.1 percentage points. Highest average does not mean winning every suite: Motus scores 97.6 on Long.

results.setting: Hammer, Bell, Card, Burger, Stand and Shoe; 500 randomized training episodes per task.
results.interpretation: Table 2 supports gains of 4.9 points over RGB-only and 4.5 over FastWAM. Figure 1 labels 92.1 instead; this report retains the detailed table's 92.2.

results.setting: Four Xtrainer tasks; approximately 100 demonstrations per task and 100 evaluation trials per task.
results.interpretation: Mask prediction improves the reported rounded average by 5.0 points over RGB-only under this protocol.

results.setting: Tasks 5–8; 60 trials per task per setting, spanning in-domain, distractors, novel instances and lighting.
results.interpretation: The 33.2-point advantage over pi0-mask is absolute, not a relative percent gain. Novel-instance transfer remains weaker than in-domain execution.

results.setting: Language-ambiguous real tasks aggregated across in-domain and out-of-domain settings.
results.comparison: No-pred keeps mask prompting but removes the future-mask target/loss. Coord keeps mask prediction but substitutes coordinate text.
results.interpretation: This supports the future-mask objective within this architecture. It does not prove that every alternative policy must predict masks.

limitations.text: Training requires mask supervision; prompted deployment depends on segmentation quality. Reliable extraction in clutter remains difficult, and large-scale joint RGB-mask-action pretraining is deferred.

Tables report no seed variability or confidence intervals, and detailed simulation evaluation counts and training-budget parity are unstated. The customized pi0-mask baseline uses additive SigLIP embedding fusion; it does not represent every possible visual-prompted VLA.

Appendix B.2 states 20 trials per task/condition, but Figure 8 contains finer-than-five-point success increments; aggregation is unexplained. IoU is measured against the original SAM3 prompt, not ground truth. Exact diagnostic rates should not be inferred.

Appendix C gives qualitative negative results without scores. Appendix A.3's blanket failure wording for coordinate baselines on Tasks 7–8 is stronger than Table 5, which includes nonzero successes. Attention examples support localization qualitatively, not a causal proof.

reproduction.text: Required components include the Wan 2.2 visual backbone, frozen causal VAE/T5, expanded RGB-mask heads, action expert, annotated action-video episodes and SAM3 prompts. Physical replication requires the Xtrainer platform with D455 head and D405 wrist cameras.

Optimizer, learning rate, batch size, training duration, GPU configuration, exact K, action representation details and denoising schedule are missing. T = 8 does not specify the action chunk length. The paper supplies no measured latency comparison for its partial-denoising claim.

Reader-proposed checks: repeat the no-pred comparison with matched data, architecture and training budget, then test equal-IoU mask shifts versus boundary distortions with fixed checkpoints. Measure target-selection and execution failures separately; these checks have not been run.

reasoning.text: WAM and object/action grounding are supported. Dual-system has architectural support from distinct visual and action experts, even though they interact inside a unified MoT. However, Eq. (1) and the three denoising losses specify joint future/action prediction, not a separately defined inverse-dynamics mapping from completed future images to actions. Deployment conditions action denoising on partially denoised latents. Thus the recorded IDM/Q4 assignment is not supported as written; joint training alone also does not justify relabeling this a single undifferentiated model.

discussionQuestions: How much of mask prediction's benefit survives an equal-capacity, equal-budget multi-seed ablation?
Does prompt location explain execution failure better than mask IoU alone?
What latency–success tradeoff does one visual denoising step produce relative to deeper denoising?

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title block and arXiv sidebar
evidence.detail: The exact title and seven authors match the catalog. The sidebar identifies arXiv:2606.13515v1, 11 June 2026; the title block says 12 June 2026. Chenghao Gu has superscript 4, but the affiliation list contains only 1, 2 and 3.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 1–2, Section 1 and Figure 1
evidence.detail: The authors motivate explicit target supervision and first-frame spatial prompts by background distraction in RGB prediction and ambiguity in language-only object selection.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Section 3 overview, Eq. (1)
evidence.detail: The conditional distribution jointly models action chunks, future RGB frames and future masks given current RGB, first-frame mask, proprioception and language; the backbone is Wan 2.2 with an MoT action expert.

evidence.location: PDF p. 3, Section 3.1, Eq. (2) and Patch embedding expansion
evidence.detail: Rendered mask images and RGB share a causal 3D VAE. Latents concatenate by channel; pretrained RGB patch weights are retained, added mask weights start at zero, and the output head expands for both latent velocities.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Figure 2(a–c) and Section 3.3
evidence.detail: The model has interacting visual and action branches. The attention matrix lets action queries attend visual tokens, while visual queries do not attend action/state tokens. The inference panel passes cached visual context to action denoising.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Section 3.2; p. 5, Implementation Details
evidence.detail: The first-frame mask is optional, is zeroed with probability 0.5 in training, and can be generated by SAM3 once at episode start. Repeated segmentation prompts are not required during deployment.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 4–5, Section 3.3, Eq. (3) and Implementation Details
evidence.detail: RGB and masks share visual timestep tau_v; actions use independently sampled tau_a. Three flow losses are summed. VAE and T5 remain frozen; input resolution is 384 by 320 in a T-shape layout and prediction horizon T is 8.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Implementation Details; p. 19, Figure 10 caption
evidence.detail: Deployment performs one joint RGB-mask denoising step and generates actions from intermediate visual context. Figure 10's fully decoded future sequences are offline visualizations only.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Performance on LIBERO; p. 6, Table 1, suite and Avg columns
evidence.detail: No test-time visual prompt is used in the stated LIBERO evaluation. Average success: full model 98.4, RGB-only 97.3, Mask-only 97.6, Motus 97.7, FastWAM 97.6. Full-model Spatial/Object/Goal/Long values are 98.8/100.0/98.2/96.4.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Table 2, caption and all method rows; p. 2, Figure 1 RoboTwin bar
evidence.detail: RoboTwin training uses 500 randomized episodes per task. Table 2 reports 92.2 average for Ours, 87.3 RGB-only, 88.8 Mask-only, 87.7 FastWAM and 72.8 pi0 over six tasks. Figure 1 instead labels Ours 92.1.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section 4.1 protocol; p. 13, Appendix A.1–A.2 and Figure 5
evidence.detail: Real-robot evaluation uses Dual-arm Xtrainer with a D455 head camera and D405 wrist cameras. Eight tasks average 100 demonstrations each. Language-clear evaluation uses 100 trials per task; ambiguous evaluation uses 60 per task per generalization setting.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Table 3; p. 13, Appendix A.2, Tasks 1–4
evidence.detail: Bowl stacking, mug hanging, drawer/pen interaction and towel folding yield 91/82/81/83 success, average 84.3. RGB-only averages 79.3, FastWAM 79.0, pi0.5 72.3 and pi0 55.8.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 6–7, Section 4.1 and Figure 4; p. 17, Table 5
evidence.detail: Tasks 5–8 test bowl, cup, bottle and cosmetic target selection. Full-model averages are 92.9 in-domain, 90.4 distractors, 74.6 novel instances and 81.7 lighting; pi0-mask gives 62.9/52.9/44.6/46.3. Figure 4 overall values are 84.9 versus 51.7/32.6/17.4 for pi0-mask/pi0-coord/FastWAM-coord.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Section 4.2 Q2–Q3 and Table 4
evidence.detail: Ours-no-pred retains the mask prompt but removes the future-mask target/loss and scores 21.6. Ours-coord retains future-mask prediction but replaces mask prompting with coordinate text and scores 18.2. Full MaskWAM scores 84.9.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 13–14, Appendix A.3, Eq. (4); p. 17, Table 5
evidence.detail: Coordinate baselines verbalize the target-mask centroid as normalized image coordinates. pi0-mask adds separately encoded RGB and mask SigLIP embeddings. Although Appendix A.3 describes failures on Tasks 7–8, Table 5 includes nonzero coordinate-baseline successes.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 14–15, Appendix B.1 and Figure 6
evidence.detail: Qwen3-VL identifies task-relevant objects for language-clear data; ambiguous data receives a human first-frame point. SAM3 propagates masks, humans verify all first-round annotations and correct poor episodes with keyframe points. Reported annotation cost is about 3 minutes per 50 episodes, with 91% requiring no correction and 5–10 extra seconds per ambiguous episode.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 15–16, Appendix B.2 and Figures 7–8
evidence.detail: Only first-frame masks are synthetically perturbed with fixed model weights on Tasks 5 and 8. The stated protocol is 20 trials per task/condition. Figure 8 uses IoU relative to the original online SAM3 mask, not ground truth; shift curves degrade more strongly. Some plotted success rates are finer than five-percentage-point increments; aggregation is not explained.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 16–17, Appendix C
evidence.detail: Authors report negative results for direct mask downsampling, a separate 3D CNN encoder, ControlNet-style injection and zero-initialized gated VLA fusion, but provide no numerical comparison for these alternatives.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Section 6; pp. 3–5, method; pp. 13–17, Appendices A–C
evidence.detail: Authors acknowledge mask-supervision and segmentation dependence and defer large-scale RGB-mask-action pretraining. Supplied implementation descriptions omit optimizer, learning rate, batch size, training steps, GPU configuration, exact action chunk length and action-sampling schedule.

evidence.location: PDF p. 18, Figure 9; p. 19, Figure 10; p. 20, Figures 11–12
evidence.detail: The appendix shows real-world rollouts, offline predicted RGB/mask futures and attention comparisons. These are qualitative examples without a quantitative attention-grounding metric.
